subject: Intermittent session splits after private cutover - holepunch/NAT mapping oddities
body:
From: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks Ops Team <ops@edgeworks.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Hi Mateo,

We completed the cutover to Redwood Private in our NYC DC over the weekend. Since then we've observed intermittent drops of long-lived websocket sessions between our mobile clients and the origin. When a session drops, clients retry and often get a new ephemeral source port mapped, which appears to break server-side affinity. The pattern repeats every ~10-30 minutes and correlates with short spikes in egress bandwidth from our gateway.

Attached: topology.png and a short pcap (sample_session_tcpdump.pcap) captured from the gateway during a reproduce window.

Quick details:
- On-prem F5 LB in front of origin (NAT at egress)
- Redwood Private peering via vxlan to our edge MR/BR with ECMP to two aggregation routers
- Clients keep a single websocket, server expects stable source port affinity (legacy behavior)

Can your team help triage whether this is a NAT sticky mapping issue vs return-path asymmetry?

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Simmons
Senior Ops Engineer, EdgeWorks

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:32:10 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Paul, thanks for the context and the captures. We'll take a look immediately.

Can you confirm: are the client retries coming from the same client IP but different source ports (i.e., ephemeral port changes)? Also please share the approximate timestamps for the pcap window in epoch or UTC.

I'm looping in Vanessa and Marissa from networking to help instrument the path and check conntrack/NAT translations.

- Mateo
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:05:42 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Paul / Mateo,

I pulled the pcap and did a quick pass. Notes below (initial triage):

Observations:
- The pcap shows client IP 198.51.100.22 making a websocket connection, then after a gap the client retries with the same source IP but a different ephemeral source port (e.g. :49872 -> :50231). The server-side conversations show the LB mapping to different SNAT tuples on the return path.
- There are short BGP reconvergence blips in the aggregation fabric around the times in the pcap (two different next-hops observed for egress within ~150ms). That coincides with the ephemeral port change and aligns with ECMP path shift.
- Conntrack entries on the Redwood egress (we pulled a remote conntrack dump, attached as conntrack-dump.txt) show both old and new tuples co-existing for brief windows, which can lead to packet re-order and perceived session break for applications that rely on stable port affinity.

Hypothesis:
- This looks like NAT mapping instability under ECMP path changes (hole-punch-like behavior). When the return path takes a different egress router, the F5 sees a different 5-tuple and applies a new SNAT mapping; the origin enforces affinity based on port and the change causes the session to be rejected until the client re-establishes.

Immediate asks / temp mitigations:
1) Can EdgeWorks configure a narrow SNAT port range per VIP on the F5 so mapping is more predictable?
2) We can temporarily pin egress for those sessions by adjusting our routing policy to prefer a single egress hop for traffic to the F5 IPs (change ECMP hash or add route-policy) — requires coordination with your network team.
3) Increase conntrack timeout for websocket-like flows on the Redwood egress to avoid premature expiry during brief path changes.

I've attached a short debug dump (debug-logs.txt) from our egress nodes showing the conntrack churn.

I'll start a ticket (INFRA-9873) and we can schedule a short maintenance window to test a pinning change.

- Vanessa
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks Ops Team <ops@edgeworks.com>, F5 Support <support@f5.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:20:05 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Vanessa, good catch on the ECMP blips. The pcap timestamps are: 2027-06-23T02:18:40Z - 02:20:10Z (gateway local time recorded as embedded).

We do have an F5 rule set that currently uses a shared port pool for SNAT. I can open a change to split that pool by VIP and allocate narrower ranges — that'll take ops lead approval but is doable.

Also worth noting: our F5 active-active pair uses route health probing and sometimes flips active path during backend slowdowns. If Redwood egress changes source port mapping when aggregated routes shift, this could produce the exact symptom.

I'll coordinate with our LB team and F5 support. In parallel, can your team confirm the feasibility of: (a) bumping conntrack timeout, (b) pinning egress to one next-hop for the F5 cluster IPs for a short window?

Thanks,
Paul

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:40:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Paul / team,

Worked through the conntrack dump and looked at our NAT translation behavior across the aggregation nodes. A few concrete notes and a playbook we can try during a short maintenance window:

Findings:
- Our kernel NAT assigns ephemeral ports from the global pool; when ECMP changes the egress interface, replies from the origin see a different source port in flight vs the conntrack expectation and the LB drops or reassigns.
- There is no per-VIP SNAT pinning currently in the path between Redwood egress and the F5.

Proposed short-term fixes (low risk):
1) Increase conntrack timeouts for ESTABLISHED websockets to 20m (currently 5m). This reduces the chance of churn during transient ECMP changes. Command: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=1200 (verify across egress nodes).
2) Add policy-based egress steering for traffic destined to the F5 cluster IPs to prefer one next-hop (temporary static route with higher priority). This is reversible and quick to test.
3) If EdgeWorks can split the SNAT port pool per VIP on their F5 we should see immediate improvement — request narrow port ranges to reduce collision probability.

Longer-term (engineering):
- We should consider configuring session-aware hashing or connection tracking handoff across aggregation nodes (conntrack sync) or enabling persistent NAT translation by VIP. Work with infra to evaluate active-active state sync options.

Action items:
- Redwood: we'll open INFRA-9873 and make the conntrack change in staging to validate. (Owner: Kimberly)
- EdgeWorks: please open the F5 change to split SNAT pools and share the proposed port ranges (Owner: Paul).
- Schedule a 30-min maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-02:30 UTC to test.

I'll prepare the playbook steps and checklist.

- Kimberly Park
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@edgeworks.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:47:03 -0400
Subject: Re: Cutover to private deployment - broken long-lived sessions

Thanks everyone. Summary / next steps:

1) Redwood (Kimberly) will push conntrack timeout bump to staging now and to prod during the scheduled window (INFRA-9873).
2) EdgeWorks (Paul) to open change for per-VIP SNAT port ranges and share ranges here; F5 Support looped for guidance.
3) Redwood (Vanessa) will add temporary egress steering for F5 IPs during the 30-min window.
4) Both sides to collect synchronized pcaps and conntrack dumps during the test to validate. Attachments above include our initial conntrack dump and debug logs.

Scheduling: proposed window 2027-06-24 02:00-02:30 UTC. Please confirm ASAP so we can staff.

I'll own coordination and the Jira ticket (JIRA-INFRA-9873).

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
